review.what_i_could_not_break:
"The round-1 metric fixes are genuinely pinned, and that is the strongest thing I found. A twenty-mutant sweep that reverts each order to the implementation it replaced (metrics-r2/mutate.py, mutate2.py) is refused by the gate in fifteen cases — leak counting `absent` as protection, residual counting `absent` as clean, form_hOUT counting or dropping `unmasked`, toolresult_masked keyed on what the mock tagged, `_span_masked` without the surviving-piece scan, `_transitions` accepting answer hops, answer_real failing only on a residual, multi_consistency counting by spelling, memory_stability wearing stability's body, coverage without the piece scan, retry_form judging only the first attempt, multi_all_out accepting any right argument, stream_fidelity over all cases, typed refusing the DOB/DATE fold. Those are real negative tests built from the reviewers' own reproductions, exactly as FIXES ordered.

The observer's needle machinery holds against everything except the derived forms: a declined name, a reformatted phone, a re-notated ISO date, a card with spaces, a by-fields address and a substitute split across two tool leaves are all found, and `own_stems` correctly stops a customer's own surname from reading as a surviving fake. `residual_answer_items` reads the whole restored reply and fires on a reformatted substitute. `merged_opcodes`' island absorption and `_merge_overlapping` do keep a rewritten name in one span in the nominative case; I only got them to split in the dative.

The report half is in good shape. new_findings.title: The entire restoration leg runs on the BASE vault while masking ran on the conversation VIEW — 33.8% of masked messages round-trip instead of 100%, and the pre-gate then calls 63% of honest answers «неверно»
new_findings.claim: `RealGateway` masks through `self._view = vault.for_conversation(conversation)` (agentpii4/gateway.py:118-123, the production `MaskContext`), but its `vault` property returns `self._base` (agentpii4/gateway.py:136) and `restore_text` is `unmask_text(text, self._base)` (agentpii4/gateway.py:248). Every v5 restoration takes that base: `answer_leg(raw_reply, case.streaming, gateway.vault, gateway.restore_text)` (harness.py:463) → the scored `reply` on an ordinary case and, on a streaming case, `stream_verdict`/`restore_stream`'s `StreamDetokenizer(base)` (harness.py:240-265); `restored_turn_replies(replies, gateway.restore_text)` (harness.py:487) → every turn the judge reads. The sidecar does the opposite: `service._scoped(org_id, conversation_id)` returns `vault.for_conversation(...)` for `/unmask`, `/unmask_chunk` and `/unmask_arguments` (pseudex/service.py:805-809, 822, 1014) — it masks and unmasks in ONE scope. Measured on the real gateway over a 400-case stratified corpus slice: of 535 masked user messages, the conversation view restores 535 (100.0%) exactly and the base restores 181 (33.8%); names and addresses do not come back at all, only digit types do. The consequence on the published lines: feeding each arm's own masked text back as the agent's confirmation, `residual_pregate_of` refuses 249/395 answers (63.0%) as «неверно» on the harness's restoration against 5/395 (1.3%) on the sidecar's. Those 249 become `judged_by="residual_gate"` rows, which `gated_answers` excludes from the calibration sample — so the human labeller can never disagree with them and κ certifies the judge on the 37% remainder. Everything downstream of the restored answer is affected: `residual`, `answer_real`, `round_trip`, `end_to_end`, `form_hOUT`, `chain_value`, the judge's whole label distribution, and `stream_fidelity` (48.8% mismatch on the base vs 78.6% on the product's own scope over 84 streaming cases, with the scored chunked text differing from what the customer reads on 32.1% of them). NOTE the tool leg is NOT affected: `restore_arguments` uses `unmask_arguments(..., self._base)` and that函 resolves correctly on the base (5.1% residual over 295 synthetic calls, r19) — the defect is confined to `unmask_text`/`StreamDetokenizer`.

new_findings.title: `--resume` with the default `--out` puts two run ids in one directory; every reader takes the alphabetically first, so the fresh calibration stamp lands in a file the report never opens
new_findings.claim: `main` defaults `out` to `runs/<today>/v5-live-<tier>` (harness.py:1034-1036) and `--resume` names a directory to read finished triples from (harness.py:1038) — so resuming the same day's run of the same tier without `--out` writes a SECOND `run_id` into the same directory. `records.merged_v5_records` globs `*.arms.v5.jsonl` and merges both (records.py:516-533), but `report.run_id_of` (report.py:208-215) and `calibration._run_id` (calibration.py:407-412) both take `sorted(glob('*.arms.jsonl'))[0]` — one id — and that id is what locates `<run>.hops.jsonl`, `<run>.judge.jsonl`, `<run>.meta.json`, `<run>.triples.jsonl`. review.what_i_could_not_break: "What held, under attack rather than by reading. (1) BLINDNESS OF THE JUDGE PROMPT. I minted substitutes through the real production path on 400+ corpus cases with `testkit.load_dev_bundle()`, hunted 25 GENUINE residuals (a minted substitute the engine's own restorer leaves standing) and grepped every built prompt under `assert_blind`'s own `_squeeze` for every minted substitute: zero hits, zero `OracleLeak`, `RESIDUAL_MARKER` present every time, `turn_residual` never zero when a residual stood. `mask_residual_turns` matches `assert_blind` exactly because `_whitespace_pattern` mirrors `_squeeze`'s whitespace collapse — the guard holds by construction, not by luck. (2) THE LEDGER'S ARITHMETIC. The judge reserves and settles inside the arms' reservation window, `triple_totals` is the single place the judge's share is computed, `charged()` rounds where the ledger rounds, and `_resume` charges the kept triples' full `cost_usd` (judge included) against the new ceiling. I could not make the file and the ledger disagree by a cent; what I broke was the unguarded reservation, not the arithmetic. (3) THE CONTROL ARMS. Both controls go through `v4_harness._guarded_arm` with v4's `PassThrough` and are written by v4's `arm_record`; `BackendV5` subclasses v4's `Backend` so the mock is shared without v5 reaching into v4's code. `pseudex_importers` parses the package with `ast` rather than grep and `test_harness.test_only_harness_imports_pseudex` holds. (4) THE TURN BOOKKEEPING. `_mcp_tools_v5`'s handler body contains no `await`, so the `sink`/`turns`/`ordinal` triple cannot interleave under concurrency; `with_streamed_answer` and `restored_turn_replies` agree on which position is the final answer because both take the last NON-EMPTY turn, and a run whose agent said nothing keeps its empty tuple rather than inventing one; `dialogue_context` drops exactly that turn, so the answer is never quoted to the judge twice and `turn_residual` cannot double-count the answer residual. (5) RECORD ROUND-TRIPS. `reply_whole`, `turn_residual`, `judge_cost_usd` all survive `records` write→read, `_scrubbed_v5_block` keeps the counts and drops the text, and a missing or non-numeric total is refused by name rather than read as zero. (6) THE RUBRIC GUARD. `form_words_in` fires at a word start over 18 stems and does not fire on «информация»; `_NOT_JUDGED` is subtracted before the check so the clause that FORBIDS judging form may keep naming склонение. (7) MECHANICAL HYGIENE: `e2e/lint_tests.py bench/agentpii5` → 0 problems, and all five tests of this lens pass. WHERE I DID NOT REACH: no live model was called, so nothing here tests the SDK transport, real `ResultMessage` cost accounting, or what a real agent writes; the `--report` replay and the v4 side-by-side belong to FIX-2's lens and I only read them where the stamp and the hop file crossed into mine."
